Dutch ( Endonym : Nederlands [ˈneːdərlɑnts] ⓘ , Nederlandse taal ) is a West Germanic language of the Indo-European language family , spoken by about 25 million people as a first language [ 4 ] and 5 million as a second language and is the third most spoken Germanic language. In Europe, Dutch is the native language of most of the population of the Netherlands and Flanders (which includes 60% of the population of Belgium ). [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Dutch was one of the official languages of South Africa until 1925, when it was replaced by Afrikaans , a separate but partially mutually intelligible daughter language [ 5 ] of Dutch. [ a ] Afrikaans, depending on the definition used, may be considered a sister language , [ 6 ] spoken, to some degree, by at least 16 million people, mainly in South Africa and Namibia , [ b ] and evolving from Cape Dutch dialects.
